thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: elevated p50/p95 latency and sustained KV prefix-cache growth on prod clusters (region: us-west-2). Auto-escalation -> oncall paged. metric: /infra/kv/prefix_count spike.

alex (eng-oncall): I'm on it — pulling logs now. tagging @maya and @jon.

maya (serving): Seeing a huge bump in unique prefix keys in the last 10m. Continuous batching queue length spiked, CPU on inference-nodes went to 95%. Also seeing lots of small differing prompt prefixes (template drift).

jon (runtime): Dumped a sample of KV keys. pattern: `prompt_prefix:<hash_v2>:<session>` — there are millions of distinct `<hash_v2>` values instead of expected ~thousands. suspect hashing/tokenizer mismatch after last tokenizer tweak.

maya (serving): Paging snippet:
```
# top keys sample (redis)
127.0.0.1:6379> ZREVRANGE prefix_index 0 20 WITHSCORES
1) "prompt_prefix:6f9d3b2a...:s"
2) "prompt_prefix:a7e12f00...:s"
...
```

alex (eng-oncall): Impact? any customer-facing 5xx? sam?

sam (support): We have 3 Priority P1 tickets reporting slow responses / timeouts for large batch generation. Errors are 504 gateway timeouts and elevated tail latency. Customers A and B on dedicated pools reported degraded throughput around 12:11 UTC.

tori (sre): Network/infra looks healthy. This is application-level amplification: small changes to prompt templates + new tokenizer -> different tokenization of leading whitespace and punctuation -> hash_v2 produced distinct keys. KV cache exploded, memory pressure triggered eviction thrashing, continuous batching tried to group many distinct prefixes -> perf cliff.

jon (runtime): Immediate mitigation plan:
1) Disable continuous batching on prod route(s) for affected models to stop batch amplification.
2) Apply temporary TTL on prefix keys to reduce keyspace growth (set 15m).
3) Rollback tokenizer change on a canary group or pin model->hash version to previous stable.
4) Run a targeted prefix key sweep to remove noisy prefixes older than 10m.

alex (eng-oncall): Agreed. I'll flip batching flag via flag service. rolling it out now.

release-bot: `deploy rollback tokenizer v2 -> v1 (canary)` started by alex at 12:18:03 UTC.

maya (serving): Batching flag changed: `continuous_batching=false` on route `generation.v1` in us-west-2. Observability: queue length dropping.

tori (sre): TTL policy applied to prefix caches: `PREFIX_TTL_SECONDS=900` (15m). Propagated to config-store.

jon (runtime): Running targeted sweep: `redis-cli --scan --pattern 'prompt_prefix:*' | while read k; do ttl=$(redis-cli TTL "$k"); if [ "$ttl" -lt 0 ]; then redis-cli EXPIRE "$k" 900; fi; done` — doing this cautiously, not mass DEL.

maya (serving): After disabling batching and TTL, CPU on nodes down to 45-55%, latency p95 improving from 3.2s -> 700ms. Error volume decreased.

sam (support): Tickets updated. Notified affected customers with status: degraded -> partial mitigation. They asked if this will recur.

alex (eng-oncall): Root cause hypothesis: tokenizer change (trim behavior + punctuation segmentation) altered prefix tokens for many templates. Hash function v2 takes raw token bytes -> produced distinct hash space. template drift + no TTL + continuous batching amplified it into a production incident.

jon (runtime): Short-term hotfix: change hashing to normalize token sequence before hashing (lowercase + normalize whitespace) and add a stable version tag to keys so we can control rollouts: `prompt_prefix:v1norm:<hash>`; preparing PR, will push to canary in 20m.

release-bot: `job 4823` started: canary rollout of runtime-hash-normalize to 3 nodes.

maya (serving): Canary looks good — no key explosion on canary nodes. Planning gradual rollout.

alex (eng-oncall): Customer impact summary for now: 2 enterprise customers with elevated latency/timeouts for ~25 minutes. No data loss, no PII exposure. SLOs breached for p95 on generation routes during the window.

tori (sre): Pager escalation: monitoring alerts remain at watch. will keep page until we have stable rollout + postmortem assignment.

sam (support): Communicated ETA to customers: full mitigation after rollout + 1 hour observation. Customers acknowledged.

jon (runtime): Rollout complete at 12:48 UTC. Post-rollout checks: unique prefix key creation rate dropped to baseline, cache cardinality stable.

maya (serving): Re-enabled controlled batching on low-traffic routes with conservative batch_size/max_latency. Not re-enabling full continuous batching until postmortem and tests.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied — batching disabled, TTL set, hash-normalize hotfix rolled to prod. Severity reduced to SEV2.

alex (eng-oncall): Taking ownership of postmortem. Will schedule a blameless review tomorrow 15:00 UTC in #incidents-postmortem. Action items for now:
- jon: finalize hash-normalize PR + add deterministic unit tests for tokenizer/hashing interactions.
- maya: add synthetic test that runs template set against tokenizer variants to detect keyspace divergence.
- tori: create alert that monitors "prefix keys per minute" and a kill-switch that disables continuous batching automatically if prefix growth delta > threshold.
- support: follow up with customers with post-incident summary.

sam (support): Will draft customer-facing timeline.

alex (eng-oncall): Handoff: I'm oncall for next 2h to watch the charts. If anything regresses, page me directly. Otherwise I'll hand off at 15:00 UTC.

incident-bot: RESOLVED: incident mitigated at 12:52 UTC. Final status: degraded -> mitigated. Postmortem scheduled.

jon (runtime): Note for postmortem: we need versioned cache keys by tokenizer/model version and tighter defaults for prefix TTLs. Also consider simulating template drift in CI.

maya (serving): Will add more telemetry (percent unique prefixes per minute, median prefix reuse window) to console dashboards.

alex (eng-oncall): Thanks all. Good catch and quick mitigation. Closing thread once postmortem doc link is up.

release-bot: `deploy` notices: none pending.

incident-bot: automated summary will be posted to #incidents-archive in 10m.
